title: Fix #10449, buffer.getBytes(...) not change a file channel position

timeline.message: Fix #10449, buffer.getBytes(...) not change a file channel position
timeline.author: Andrey Mizurov

timeline.body:
Motivation:

Regression appeared after making changes in fix #10360 .
The main problem here that `buffer.getBytes(buffer.readerIndex(), fileChannel, fileChannel.position(), localsize)`
doesn't change channel position after writes.

Modification:

Manually set position according to the written bytes.

Result:

Fixes #10449 .

reply.body: @amizurov I think @njhill is right here... can you adjust this please ?
Sure, according java docs it depends on implementation.
instead of `if (written > 0)`, you might better inverse the test to `if (written < 0)` which stands for end of file/channel, therefore giving a break of the `while` loop ?

or `if (written <= 0)` since the javadoc does not specify negative result (as in standard Java interaction with file or stream). The idea is to have a clear "break" code, and therefore to not rely only on while condition.
I changed code according suggestion but i'm not sure is it ok if we break from loop but possible not all data is written or maybe i'm confused :)
@amizurov I think we should only break on `< 0` as `0` is valid.
